title: Accuracy
description: Simple correctness rate on classification or multiple-choice tasks.
protocol: Fixed shots, greedy decoding, pinned harness version.
limitations: Says nothing about calibration, reasoning, or open-ended quality. Gameable by memorization.

title: Perplexity
description: Exp(mean cross-entropy loss)). Lower is better. Standard for language modeling.
whenToUse: Measuring language modeling quality. Comparing models on the same test set.
protocol: Same tokenizer and test set for every comparison; report train and val separately.
limitations: Weights all tokens equally; correlates imperfectly with task success. Never sufficient alone.

title: MMLU
description: Measurements of 57 subjects (math, history, law, medicine, etc.) in multiple-choice format.
whenToUse: Broad knowledge assessment. The most commonly reported benchmark.
protocol: Standard 5-shot; report per-subject slices, not just the mean.
limitations: Widely contaminated (web text includes test items); saturated at the top; multiple-choice format rewards memorization.

title: GSM8K
description: 8.5K grade-school math word problems. Tests mathematical reasoning.
protocol: 8-shot chain-of-thought or strict exact-match; extract the last number.
limitations: Small (8.5k items, test 1.3k) - noisy deltas; heavily represented in web data (contamination risk).

title: HellaSwag
description: Commonsense reasoning: complete the sentence given a context from activity descriptions.
protocol: Zero/few-shot fixed; watch for length-bias artifacts.
limitations: Nearing saturation; adversarial filtering artifacts; weak signal for instruction-tuned models.

title: TruthfulQA
description: Tests whether models reproduce common misconceptions or provide truthful answers.
whenToUse: Evaluating truthfulness and resistance to misinformation.
protocol: Zero-shot; both multiple-choice and open generation.
limitations: Small; measures misconception avoidance, not general honesty; judge-dependent on the generation track.

title: IFEval
description: Instruction following evaluation: can the model follow exact constraints in prompts?
protocol: Verifiable constraints (length, format, keywords); deterministic checking.
limitations: Covers only mechanically verifiable instructions - a slice of real instruction following.

title: HumanEval
description: Python coding tasks. Measure pass@k: can the model generate correct code?
protocol: Greedy or low-temp samples; sandboxed execution of hidden tests.
limitations: 164 tasks - high variance; Python-only; execution environment must be sandboxed and pinned.

title: Custom Task Evaluation
description: Your own held-out set mirroring production traffic - the only eval that measures your claim.
metric: Task-defined (rubric score, exact match, win rate vs baseline).
protocol: Locked before training; 200+ items for reasonable error bars; baselines included.
limitations: Incomparable externally; costs effort to build and label. Worth it anyway.

title: LLM-as-Judge
description: A strong model scores outputs against a rubric for open-ended quality.
whenToUse: Summarization, chat quality, style - where exact match fails.
metric: Rubric score or pairwise win rate.
protocol: Fixed rubric + few-shot anchors; calibrate against 50+ human grades (target kappa 0.7+); cross-family judges.
limitations: Self-preference, length bias, and prompt sensitivity. A noisy instrument - report agreement, never trust raw.
